articles/atomic-original-directory-delet.title: Atomic original directory deletion | MirrorPulse Adapter SDK documentation
articles/atomic-original-directory-delet.summary: Atomic original directory deletion Use this optional path only when the backend can make every original removal and its effect receipt visible in one durable transaction. If it can commit only one child at a time, see admission and child effects. A backend that can commit a whole admitted subtree in one native transaction can offer atomic-original-directory-delete-v1, in addition to original-directory-admission-v1. This does not enable the separate individual child or final-directory effect capabilities. Opt in during negotiation. DeleteOriginalDirectoryAtomically returns OriginalDirectoryDeletedAtomically; ordinary MutationComplete is insufficient. Validate and reserve the admitted plan The request includes the complete original admission request and backend admission, and binds their fingerprints to the Host's sealed manifest. All operations must be conditional Delete operations in the admitted leaf-first order. Move, upload and directory creation are outside this capability. A staged cross-instance move may use this operation for source retirement only after the Host has durably verified the complete destination copy and authorized every source operation. The capability itself supplies no copy or verification proof. The backend revalidates its durable admission, complete inventory, original generations and conditions under the same qualified history and exclusion boundary as its native transaction. It reserves the immutable Host authorization before source mutation. The same admission or any of its operation IDs cannot be rebound to another plan, manifest or individual-effect execution. Capability negotiation, hashes and SDK shape checks cannot establish these native facts. Commit, reply and recover All original removals and one immutable receipt commit together. No child result is returned or counted as accepted before the batch commits. The receipt retains every operation ID, original address and original generation in the authorized order, as well as the request, admission and manifest fingerprints and backend commit evidence. It is a whole-batch receipt; it is not a chain of provisional AdapterOwnedChildEffectReceipt values. It has no fabricated deletion revision. Before commit, cancellation or process death must preserve every original and leave no accepted receipt. After commit, a lost reply, cancellation or process restart must recover the identical receipt without opening or mutating a later occupant at the original path. The backend refuses changed authorization and missing, corrupt or incompatible retained evidence. Host acknowledgement follows durable acceptance of the full receipt and remains a separate product step. For a backend qualification, interrupt execution once before commit and once after commit but before replying. Before commit, verify the entire original inventory and the absence of an accepted receipt. After commit, restart and replay the unchanged request. Verify that its receipt is identical and that a later object created at an old path is untouched. Also replay with a changed manifest and verify that the backend refuses it without applying any effects. AdapterAtomicDirectoryDeletionWire checks protocol, both capabilities, request/session/instance correlation, a 1 MiB body limit and exact reply membership. The dispatcher validates before invoking IAdapterAtomicDirectoryDeletionBackend and validates its reply. Signed Host/Worker integration must separately qualify durability, native history/exclusion, root authorization and official journal ACK. The SDK contract checks use a synthetic backend and do not claim those outcomes.

articles/getting-started.html.title: Getting started | MirrorPulse Adapter SDK documentation
articles/getting-started.html.summary: Getting started Build the template first so you have a known working package. Then replace its in-memory backend one operation at a time and try the resulting Worker in MirrorPulse. Prerequisites PowerShell 7 and the .NET SDK selected in the template's global.json. A Windows x64 or ARM64 machine to run a matching Worker. The shell launcher on macOS or Linux can cross-build both Windows payloads. A disposable MirrorPulse setup and a storage fixture you control for Host and provider tests. 1. Build the template Create a repository from the Adapter template and clone your new repository. Run Build-Adapter.cmd on Windows or ./build-adapter.sh on Linux or macOS. From PowerShell, you can specify a development version. pwsh ./Build-Adapter.ps1 -Version 1.0.0-preview.1 The launcher prints the path of the .mpadapter below artifacts/release. It builds the same package for both Windows architectures and uses a disposable test key. Only a Host configured to trust that signer can install it. The signed package and its companion signature should stay together. 2. Give the package its own identity and settings File in the template What to change eng/release-manifest.json Set the canonical Adapter ID, publisher, root key, and protocol and package metadata. Keep the Adapter ID and root key stable after publication. template/package/forms/config.xml Declare the per-deployment connection settings the Host collects and mark them required or optional. template/package/locales/en-US.json Define the English title, description, field labels, option labels and image text. template/package/assets/logo.png Supply your own local logo and update the manifest path if it changes. samples/MirrorPulse.Adapter.SampleWorker/ Replace the sample’s in-memory storage implementation. Retain the SDK-based process and frame handling. Start with a plain endpoint field and a password field if the backend requires credentials. Add localized help explaining the expected endpoint format. The Host presents the form and stores its values, including credentials. Read normal settings and opaque credential references when the Host starts the Worker. See Package configuration for complete examples. 3. Add the first storage operations Use a small fixture you control. Implement listing and stat first. Follow with a bounded range read so MirrorPulse can read the content of a listed file. Return the selected root key on every operation, keep directory cursors scoped to their directory, and surface a revision mismatch as a conflict. With writes enabled, exercise retries using the original operation ID and verify what happens after the connection or Worker stops. Follow Implement a Worker for the message sequence. 4. Try a signed package in MirrorPulse Build the package again and install it using Adapter management, or run MirrorPulse adapter install C:/path/to/your-adapter.mpadapter from an edition that trusts your test signer. Create a deployment for the installed version. Enter the required form values, save them, then enable the deployment if it is disabled. Verify that the Host starts the Worker and the root shows only the configured fixture. Read a small file through MirrorPulse and compare the bytes with the source. If the Adapter supports writes, verify one change through MirrorPulse and check the backend. Stop and reopen the Host. The deployment should keep its configuration, and reconnecting should preserve its scope. Verify the actual published package separately from source or test-key packages. See Test and publish an Adapter. Run the SDK sample independently If you cloned the SDK repository, run the following from its root. Its in-memory Worker and contract executable demonstrate the process protocol. dotnet restore MirrorPulse.Adapter.sln --locked-mode dotnet build MirrorPulse.Adapter.sln -c Release --no-restore dotnet run --project tests/MirrorPulse.Adapter.ContractTests -c Release --no-build

articles/implementing-a-worker.html.title: Implement a Worker | MirrorPulse Adapter SDK documentation
articles/implementing-a-worker.html.summary: Implement a Worker The Worker runs locally as a separate process. It keeps backend-specific connection logic behind the SDK types. MirrorPulse owns the deployment lifetime, settings, credential store and the Windows Cloud Files session. Use the Worker protocol for the precise field, frame size and binary layout rules. Start and stop a session Step Worker responsibility Launch Parse AdapterWorkerProcessArguments, connect with AdapterNamedPipeClient, and create an AdapterControlChannel scoped to the instance and session. Hello Send a bootstrap Hello with the supported versions and offered capabilities. Keep its request ID for the matching response. Ready Check the matching response and run AdapterHandshake.ValidateReady. Call SelectProtocol only after validation. Use only the selected capabilities. Bind Resolve the authorized root and its settings. For a password field, use the reference in Ready.CredentialBindings on the established channel. A disabled root must not connect to storage. Connected Send the event with a fresh request ID when the normal storage session is ready. Stop or disconnect Release streams and temporary transfer leases. Use a new session for the next launch. Keep a single frame reader and serialize complete writes. In-flight upload handling must still accept a matching cancellation command. Credentials and raw backend errors should stay out of responses and ordinary logs. Package configuration describes the separate startup mode for authorization callbacks before a root exists. List, stat and read files Use AdapterFileAddress for root-qualified addresses. Validate the authorized root key and relative path before accessing the backend. The empty path identifies the root. Map the address to the provider's native namespace without permitting aliases or paths that leave the configured root. List returns at most the requested page size and binds any continuation cursor to the root and parent directory. Every incomplete page carries a next cursor. Specify how your backend behaves when the directory changes while paging. Stat returns the current revision or the protocol's absent result. Decide whether a revision represents a server generation, a content hash, or a weaker metadata observation. Document the distinction. ReadRange checks a supplied revision and returns one bounded range. Send the matching ReadRangeReady followed by the final v2 binary chunk. Keep the declared length, offset, session, stream and root consistent. For providers that send changes, keep change-feed cursors separate from directory-list cursors. State their scope, retention and recovery behavior. An expired cursor needs an explicit invalidation or reconciliation path consistent with the negotiated feed. Apply a mutation and recover a lost reply A request ID identifies one transport exchange. A stable operation ID identifies the mutation across retries. Retain the source and destination addresses, conditions, and effective content identity in its binding. A repeated ID with changed inputs is an error. An accepted retry should recover the original receipt or report that the outcome is unknown. A fresh request ID alone gives no evidence that a prior operation failed. For a conditional upload, validate the operation and its preconditions, receive the declared bounded stream into a transfer lease, then verify the bytes before publication. Validate the offset and checksum of each chunk. Use the backend's conditional operation when available and report unsupported conditions before changing storage. The SDK's frame, address and lease types do not give a storage backend compare-and-swap or durable replay by themselves. A cancellation during receive releases the lease before acknowledging cancellation. If the remote mutation already committed or its response was lost, use the stable operation binding to determine recovery. Never adopt a response from a previous Worker session. Add optional features deliberately Offer structured health, update discovery or authorization callbacks if the Worker actually implements them. Treat the original-directory admission, retirement and atomic deletion protocols as separate capabilities. They require native history, exclusion and durable effect evidence in addition to the SDK wire validation.

articles/index.html.title: Adapter SDK documentation | MirrorPulse Adapter SDK documentation
articles/index.html.summary: Adapter SDK documentation A MirrorPulse deployment connects one configured storage root to a Worker. The same Adapter package can serve several independent deployments. MirrorPulse starts a separate process and supplies settings and credential references for each deployment. Build your first Adapter Getting started walks through the template, the package files to edit, and the first deployment. Package configuration covers the signed manifest, the localized XML form, saved settings and credentials, authorization callbacks, health reports and version offers. Implement a Worker covers the process handshake, addresses, listing and ranged reads, uploads, mutation replay and cancellation. Test and publish an Adapter shows what the SDK runner verifies and what to check against an actual backend and MirrorPulse Host. Protocol and API Use the wire specification for envelope and binary field definitions, including the versioned examples beside it. Use the API reference for the .NET types that implement those contracts. The following optional protocols require backend-specific evidence and durability. Implement ordinary file operations before assessing them. Guide Purpose Original directory admission Preserve the original subtree identity and the ordered, conditional plan before committing any child effect. Original directory retirement Verify the accepted child history and retire the original directory using its retained evidence. Atomic original directory deletion Commit and recover one qualified deletion of the whole admitted original subtree. SDK trusted publishing is the maintainer guide for publishing the SDK and its matching wire specification and conformance tools.

articles/nuget-publishing.html.title: SDK trusted publishing | MirrorPulse Adapter SDK documentation
articles/nuget-publishing.html.summary: SDK trusted publishing Use this procedure when publishing the SDK itself. Adapter authors publish their Workers through the Adapter package workflow. A single SDK release binds NuGet, the wire specification and the native conformance tools to the same source commit. Configure GitHub and NuGet Configure trusted publishing on nuget.org for the MirrorPulse.Adapter.Sdk package. Match the names in this table to the GitHub release workflow. Field Stable Preview Repository owner MirrorPulse MirrorPulse Repository adapter-sdk adapter-sdk Workflow file sdk-release.yml sdk-release.yml Environment stable preview Package pattern MirrorPulse.Adapter.Sdk MirrorPulse.Adapter.Sdk Restrict the stable environment to main and the preview environment to develop. Require a stable reviewer and disable self-review. Set the NUGET_USER secret to the owning NuGet profile name. The workflow exchanges GitHub OIDC for a temporary NuGet credential after the candidate passes conformance on both Windows architectures and the environment approves publication. Configure trusted publishing Qualify and publish one candidate Set the SDK version in src/MirrorPulse.Adapter.Sdk/MirrorPulse.Adapter.Sdk.csproj. Dispatch SDK Release from develop for a version with a preview.N suffix, or from protected main for a stable version. The default dispatch builds the package, specification and both native runners, then runs conformance against those exact artifacts. To publish, enable publish and enter PUBLISH in the confirmation field. NuGet and GitHub receive the same candidate from the workflow artifact. GitHub retains the original length, SHA256 and source commit in sdk-release.json. If one destination accepts the version and the other fails, recover using the original artifact and source evidence before changing the version or rebuilding it. Check the published SDK version in the NuGet package listing and the GitHub tag. Verify the package and companion archives against the release inventory before updating consumer lock files. The GitHub release contains the exact package used for the fixed-hash feed, the protocol specification, and one standalone runner for each supported architecture. Diagnose a failed release Where it stopped What to inspect Version or source resolution Check the project version, selected branch and channel. The version cannot replace an existing published version. Native conformance Read the failed architecture's evidence. Fix source and qualify a new candidate before publishing. Environment or OIDC Check the environment review and its branch restrictions. Match the workflow filename, repository identity and NuGet owner against the configured policy. One destination published Hold the candidate artifact and its hashes. Check which destination already accepted those bytes, then use those exact bytes to finish recovery. The public documentation has its own workflow. Documentation-only fixes can deploy to the site through main without creating a new SDK package version.

articles/original-directory-admission-wi.title: Original directory admission and child effects | MirrorPulse Adapter SDK documentation
articles/original-directory-admission-wi.summary: Original directory admission and child effects Use this protocol when a backend can identify the complete original subtree, observe native generations, and verify each child effect against a durable admission. Workers with only ordinary file commands can leave this capability unselected. Read Implement a Worker for the shared session and operation rules. Admit the original plan A Worker negotiates original-directory-admission-v1 before accepting AdmitOriginalDirectory, which returns OriginalDirectoryAdmitted. Individual ApplyOriginalChild / OriginalChildApplied exchanges additionally require original-directory-effects-v1 and original-directory-child-effects-v1. The existing RetireOriginalDirectory message completes an admitted directory after its children under its existing effects capability. Admission alone grants neither mutation path. The Host sends the original instance, admission ID and complete ordered source operations. Every entry retains its stable operation ID, address, explicit revision condition, destination for a move and absence condition. Children precede their direct parent and all paths form one connected subtree. Move destinations leave that original subtree. The request fingerprint covers the entire ordered plan. The plan has at most 2048 operations. The backend checks its complete inventory and original conditions and persists the admission before replying. The reply binds each operation to its original generation, a directory witness where appropriate and the exact source and destination parent witnesses. Witnesses retain the admission request fingerprint. The admission fingerprint covers those observations. Duplicate requests recover that same admission. A changed request or incomplete inventory is refused. The backend retains the stable operation claims across admissions. Apply a child and extend the parent history Each file effect request retains the admission and Host manifest fingerprints, original operation and generation, original parent witnesses and the previously accepted receipt for each affected parent. Its fingerprint includes these bindings. The backend validates the request against its durable admission and checks each predecessor against its accepted effect ledger. Shape validation by itself cannot establish those backend facts. The backend binds the Host manifest once per admission and requires the same binding for every child effect and final directory retirement. The typed child receipt binds the full request fingerprint, original generation and exact before/after transitions for each original parent. The first effect starts from the admitted revision. Later effects extend the previously accepted receipt. A deletion's accepted revision is null. The backend commits the native effect and durable receipt together and returns that receipt after a lost reply or process restart. The Host persists the same receipt before advancing its plan. For example, a plan deleting incoming/first.txt, then incoming/second.txt, then incoming starts the first child at the admitted revision of incoming. Its receipt accounts for the first parent revision change. The second child must extend that receipt, so a later version caused by an unrelated writer cannot become its starting point. The final retirement uses both accepted children and their resulting revision. Integrate and exercise recovery AdapterOriginalDirectoryWire validates protocol, negotiated capabilities, bounded payloads and request/session/instance correlation. Each body is limited to 1 MiB. AdapterOriginalDirectoryDispatcher decodes before calling the backend and validates the backend reply before returning a control frame. A Worker can route these messages from its existing control reader to an IAdapterOriginalDirectoryBackend implementation. An admission-only backend can implement IAdapterOriginalDirectoryAdmissionBackend; the dispatcher refuses individual effects when that implementation is unavailable. Backend implementations also own root authorization, native path rules, complete history, exclusion during validation and mutation, and crash recovery. The dispatcher supports protocol validation around that implementation. Production enablement requires signed Host and Worker qualification of the complete admitted operation and official journal acknowledgement. A backend that only commits an entire original subtree atomically can use the separately negotiated atomic deletion contract. It must not return an individual child receipt while that child's native transaction can still roll back.

articles/original-directory-retirement-w.title: Original directory retirement messages | MirrorPulse Adapter SDK documentation
articles/original-directory-retirement-w.summary: Original directory retirement messages This optional protocol-v2 exchange is the final step after a qualified backend has verified the original subtree and recorded its child effects. The SDK defines the request and response. Backend support and production Host qualification are required before it can acknowledge an original operation. The sample Worker does not implement this capability. The negotiated capability is original-directory-effects-v1. The new request message is RetireOriginalDirectory; its successful response message is OriginalDirectoryRetired. Ordinary Delete, Move and MutationComplete messages cannot stand in for these messages. Protocol 1, absent capability, unknown versions and differently cased capability names are refused. Request AdapterDirectoryRetirementRequest contains the final nonrecursive Delete or Move of one original directory. It retains: The immutable operation ID, exact source address, destination for a move, and explicit source revision precondition. The complete AdapterDirectoryRetirementEvidence: original directory witness, sealed manifest fingerprint, required direct-child operations, chronologically accepted child receipts and the terminal owned directory revision. The exact original source and destination direct-parent witnesses. The source parent's generation must equal the admitted directory's parent generation. Each available original parent predecessor receipt, separately from the child ledger. One parent may have at most one predecessor; a receipt that affects both parents may be supplied once. No foreign, duplicate or unrelated receipt can become the basis of a new parent transition. A canonical SHA-256 fingerprint of all these fields. Required-child set and parent ordering are canonical; accepted-child chronology remains significant. The source precondition must equal the child ledger's final expected revision. It cannot be absent, replaced by a current Stat, or silently taken from a later object. The final operation cannot reuse a child operation ID. The source cannot be a configured root; a move cannot replace a destination, target a configured root, or move into its own subtree. Backends must additionally apply their native path normalization and alias rules. An author constructs the retained request and uses CalculateFingerprint() to bind it. Every decoder revalidates the complete request. Recalculating a hash is not permission to rebase retained state or replace an original child manifest. Witness provenance and sealed-manifest ownership remain backend/Host duties. Response and recovery The response payload is the existing AdapterOwnedChildEffectReceipt, with the exact request fingerprint, operation, admission, instance, original directory generation, source and destination. It must contain precisely the admitted direct-parent transitions. Each transition extends the retained predecessor; without a predecessor it starts at the original parent revision and has no predecessor fingerprint. A deletion's accepted revision remains null. AdapterDirectoryRetirementWire.ReadRequest and ReadResponse validate the payload and envelope. Responses must match the request ID, Worker session, instance, protocol and response role. Each payload is limited to 1 MiB, below the existing outer frame limit. A null or ordinary mutation response is not evidence of retirement. These checks grant no native mutation authority. A capable backend still needs to verify original identity/history and the complete child manifest under its atomicity or exclusion mechanism; commit effects and durable receipts together; and recover a lost reply without touching a later tree. The Host must persist and compare the exact receipt before advancing its ledger or acknowledging an original journal operation. Unsupported backends leave the original pending. The bounded request does not introduce manifest paging; an oversized admission requires explicit refusal rather than truncation. Verify the final effect Start with an admitted directory and retain its original witnesses. Test a successful retirement with zero children, another with several recorded child effects, and rejection after an unrelated writer changes a parent. Drop the reply after the native effect commits, restart the Worker, and retry with the original evidence. The same receipt should be recovered. An unrelated object at the old name must remain outside the operation. The contract executable exercises encoded control-frame round trips, complete child chains, exact parent predecessors, Delete and cross-root Move responses, null revisions, changed bindings, replay-correlation mistakes, downgrade and payload limits. These are SDK wire-boundary checks, not a claim that a live Worker/backend or recursive Host acceptance is complete.

articles/package-configuration.html.title: Package configuration contract | MirrorPulse Adapter SDK documentation
articles/package-configuration.html.summary: Package configuration contract SDK 1.0 packages use manifest schema 2. Keep one rootDefinitions item and set instancePolicy.maximumRootDefinitions to 1. One Adapter package can still be installed in multiple deployments. Use a canonical lowercase Adapter ID and a three-part stable or -preview.N package version. Package identity and files Start from the template's eng/release-manifest.json. The package ID identifies the Adapter across versions. The root key identifies its declared root and must stay stable for deployments that will upgrade in place. The root label and directory name supply presentation defaults. The actual deployment display name is saved by the Host. Use separate IDs for separate Adapters, even if they share a storage library. Package the Worker entrypoints and their private runtime under the matching win-x64 and win-arm64 manifest keys. Declare protocol 2 and the capabilities the backend actually supports. Declaring a package capability does not select a wire feature. The Worker still negotiates wire capabilities at startup. Localized presentation and forms Use presentation for the package title, description, logo, and form. These are separate from the stable Adapter ID. { "presentation": { "titleKey": "package.title", "descriptionKey": "package.description", "logoPath": "assets/logo.png", "formPath": "forms/config.xml" }, "locales": ["en-US"], "localeMetadata": { "en-US": { "displayName": "English (United States)", "resourcePath": "locales/en-US.json" } } } Include each referenced file in the signed package inventory, with the exact same spelling and case. Resource paths use / and are relative to the package root. Images use PNG, JPEG, ICO or BMP. Locale files are flat JSON objects that map label keys to display text. The en-US table covers every label used in the form and presentation. A selected locale can omit keys to use the corresponding English text. The separate form is declarative XML. Its supported layout items are heading, paragraph and image. Every image requires a localized accessibility label. Field keys remain stable across releases. The form also supports the following editable controls and callback buttons. <form version="1"> <heading textKey="setup.title" /> <paragraph textKey="setup.instructions" /> <image path="assets/logo.png" altKey="package.title" /> <text key="endpoint" labelKey="field.endpoint" required="true" /> <password key="accessToken" labelKey="field.accessToken" required="false" /> <singleChoice key="mode" labelKey="field.mode" required="true" default="read"> <option id="read" labelKey="mode.read" /> <option id="write" labelKey="mode.write" /> </singleChoice> <multiChoice key="scopes" labelKey="field.scopes" required="false" default="read,write"> <option id="read" labelKey="mode.read" /> <option id="write" labelKey="mode.write" /> </multiChoice> <checkBox key="enabled" labelKey="field.enabled" required="false" default="true" /> <callback id="authorize" labelKey="action.authorize"> <write key="accessToken" /> <write key="scopes" /> </callback> </form> Use stable field keys, option IDs, and callback IDs independent of display language. The form requires a true or false value for each field's required attribute. Defaults are optional. Password fields cannot declare defaults. A single choice default names one option ID. Multiple choice defaults use comma-separated IDs and an empty default selects nothing. Check box defaults are true or false. AdapterPackageMetadata.Read validates the versioned package metadata against the signed file inventory. AdapterConfigurationForm.Read validates the layout, field bindings and callback write declarations. AdapterConfigurationTranslations.Read verifies the fallback string table and resolves display labels. These methods operate on parsed metadata and package data supplied by the caller. The Host validates the signature and continues to own configuration, authorization transactions, validation and persistence. A callback's write list is the maximum set of fields the Host may accept from that callback. Settings and credentials The Host renders the form and owns Save. Ordinary controls contribute values under their field keys. Choice values use option IDs, even when their labels change with the language. Multi-choice selects comma-separated IDs and a check box contributes true or false. Validate backend-specific combinations, such as credentials required only for a selected authentication mode, when reading settings. Keep help text and validation tied to field keys. A password control is a secret field. For a one-root deployment, read its opaque reference from Ready.CredentialBindings, indexed by field key, and use a correlated credential request on the established channel. A reference is an identifier, so sending it as a password will fail. Keep returned secret values in memory only and keep them out of config files, diagnostics and error payloads. The Worker can report a missing or expired password with structured health if it implements that capability. Keep existing field and choice IDs stable across updates. Changing a label keeps the saved value. Introducing a new required field can leave an existing deployment needing user input. Exercise that case and use a field-keyed health issue where the Worker can identify the missing value. Authorization, health and updates Configuration-only Worker startup MirrorPulse can start the signed Worker before any deployment exists and can use the same mode to reauthorize an existing deployment. Parse the usual AdapterWorkerProcessArguments and inspect ConfigurationOnly. In that mode, advertise AdapterConfigurationCallbackContract.Capability with protocol 2, then validate the Host's Ready with that launch mode. The accepted Ready has zero root bindings and includes the settings available for this authorization. Keep the normal sync handshake and startup path when ConfigurationOnly is false. var arguments = AdapterWorkerProcessArguments.Parse(args); var offer = new AdapterHello(new(2, 2), arguments.ConfigurationOnly ? [AdapterConfigurationCallbackContract.Capability] : AdapterHandshake.V2Capabilities); // Send Hello and decode its matching Ready response as AdapterReady. AdapterHandshake.ValidateReady(ready, offer, arguments.ConfigurationOnly); channel.SelectProtocol(ready.SelectedVersion); In configuration-only mode, handle ConfigurationCallbackStart, ConfigurationCallbackPoll, ConfigurationCallbackCancel, and the Host's Stop. Read callback messages with AdapterConfigurationCallbackContract.ReadRequest after reading the frame from AdapterControlChannel. Track the invocation ID, callback ID and expiry in memory for this session. Send ConfigurationCallbackResult as a response with the matching frame request ID. A pending response can include an HTTPS authorization page. A Worker that owns its own interaction window can return pending without a URL. A successful response proposes values only for fields listed in the callback's signed write list. Cancel ends the interaction and discards proposed writes. AdapterReady.CredentialBindings indexes opaque Host credential references by password field key. For an existing deployment, a Worker can use a supplied reference with a CredentialRequest and read its matching CredentialResponse on the authenticated channel. Password values stay out of ordinary configuration and logs. Use the temporary cache directories supplied by the Host and keep authorization state in memory. MirrorPulse accepts authorized writes when the user saves the form, stores passwords in its credential store and ends the temporary Worker session. Send file operations, directory state and change notifications from the normal sync session. Health and updates Offer AdapterDeploymentContract.StructuredHealthCapability when the Worker can identify configuration and credential issues. If the ordinary deployment's Ready selects that capability, send the complete AdapterHealthReport as a protocol 2 notification with AdapterDeploymentContract.HealthReportMessage, a fresh frame request ID, and isResponse: false. It can arrive before Connected when a credential blocks startup. Replace the report as conditions change, and send an empty issue list after recovery. Include the exact signed form field key when known. Credential issues can name password fields. Source and Worker failures carry no field. Keep the report within 16 unique issues and keep arbitrary diagnostic text and credential values out of it. Update checks are optional. A Worker can include update-discovery in its protocol 2 Hello and check that Ready selects it. After Connected, the Host can send CheckAdapterUpdate with an empty object. Reply with AdapterUpdateOffer using the same request, instance and session identifiers. This exchange applies to the selected deployment and carries no rootKey. Serialize AdapterPackageUpdateResult as the response payload. Set Offer to null when the selected package is current. Otherwise, offer the same Adapter ID, a strictly newer version, and an HTTPS URL or the absolute path of a local Windows .mpadapter file, represented as a file: URI. HTTPS packages carry an embedded signature. The Host asks the user before acquiring the package and checks its signature and identity before registering the version. Users can then select that version for each deployment.

articles/test-and-publish.html.summary: Test and publish an Adapter Use the SDK contracts for shared wire behavior and a disposable backend to prove the actual provider behavior. Build the release once and keep the exact signed payload through both native qualification runs and publication. Run the shared and provider tests Run pwsh ./eng/verify.ps1 in a project created from the Adapter template. For SDK development, use the contract executable. The SDK release provides a standalone runner for Windows x64 and ARM64. Download the matching runner and specification from the fixed SDK release and verify their lengths and SHA-256 values in sdk-release.json. The runner's single-root profile uses a controlled memory-source fixture. For a compatible test Worker with a root key of sample, use the following from PowerShell on a Windows runner of the matching architecture. $worker = 'C:/fixture/worker/Worker.exe' $cache = Join-Path ([IO.Path]::GetTempPath()) ([Guid]::NewGuid().ToString('N')) New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path $cache | Out-Null ./MirrorPulse.Adapter.Conformance.exe --worker $worker --transfer-cache $cache --single-root sample The Worker must supply the expected fixture contents, including readme.txt with UTF-8 content Memory source: sample followed by a newline. The default runner mode checks the separate legacy multiple-root fixture; independent SDK 1.0 packages should use the single-root profile where applicable. A provider with different fixture semantics should supply an equivalent process-level suite. Qualify a real deployment Verify Observe Startup and isolation The exact package is accepted by a Host that trusts its signer. The correct native executable and private runtime start. Two deployments of the same package use separate configuration, credentials and state. Read path Nested directories and multiple pages enumerate correctly. Range bytes match the fixture. A stale revision, wrong root and invalid cursor are refused. Writes, if supported Preconditions are checked; disallowed moves fail; interrupted uploads release the cache; lost replies and restart preserve operation identity and recover a receipt or an explicit unknown outcome. Failure and recovery Restart or disconnect during an operation, reconnect with the same deployment, and verify that changes apply only to the intended source. Configuration Required fields are enforced. Passwords and authorization results survive a Host restart via the Host credential store. Optional health and update features report their actual state. Use disposable endpoints and clean directories. Record the exact source commit, candidate package hash, architecture and observed results. A wire conformance pass alone only qualifies the tested wire profile. Package and sign a release A release package declares one root and includes both win-x64 and win-arm64 entrypoints, local metadata assets, its Worker dependencies, and required notices. Keep package ID, root key, persistent field keys and option IDs stable when you publish a compatible update. Use the template’s protected publication workflow for your repository. Use the development launcher for test-signed packages. Production validation needs the intended production signer and an installation with the production trust policy. Retain the package bytes and companion signature together. Keep installed versions immutable and publish changed bytes under a new version. If the Worker implements update discovery, return only a newer version of the same Adapter. MirrorPulse verifies the download and lets a user choose when to move an existing deployment to it. Publishing the SDK itself is documented under SDK trusted publishing.

index.html.summary: How to build an Adapter An Adapter connects a storage backend to MirrorPulse. It ships as a signed .mpadapter containing a Windows Worker, its private runtime, and a description of the settings MirrorPulse should collect. The Adapter SDK provides the public .NET contract and conformance tools. The Adapter template is the starting repository for a new implementation. Start here Use it to Adapter template Build a runnable example, then replace the sample storage implementation. Getting started Follow the template from first build to installation and a working deployment. Package configuration Define a package, localize its form, bind credentials, and add optional authorization, health or update support. Implement a Worker Implement the pipe lifecycle, file operations, consistency checks and recovery. Test and publish an Adapter Qualify the Worker and the exact signed package on x64 and ARM64. API reference Find the generated reference for the public SDK types. Build your first package Create a repository from the Adapter template. Install PowerShell 7 and the .NET SDK selected by the template's global.json. Run Build-Adapter.cmd on Windows or ./build-adapter.sh on macOS or Linux. The launcher builds the x64 and ARM64 Windows payloads and signs a development package using a disposable test key. The command prints the package path under artifacts/release. Edit eng/release-manifest.json for package identity and the root definition. Edit template/package/forms/config.xml, template/package/locales/en-US.json and template/package/assets/logo.png for settings and presentation. Replace the sample Worker in samples/MirrorPulse.Adapter.SampleWorker. Start with a real listing and bounded read, then add write operations only where your backend can honor the requested preconditions. Test the signed package with an appropriate trust configuration in a disposable MirrorPulse environment. Create a deployment, save its configuration, and verify the Worker reads a file from its configured source. An SDK 1.0 package declares one root. A package can have several deployments, each with its own settings, credential references and Worker session. The Host owns the Windows sync root, configuration persistence and credentials. The Worker translates between the selected protocol and its storage backend. Work on the SDK itself The public NuGet package is MirrorPulse.Adapter.Sdk 1.0.0. SDK releases also publish the versioned specification and native conformance tools. Use the Worker protocol for wire field definitions or when implementing a Worker in another language. From this repository, use the .NET SDK selected in global.json. dotnet restore MirrorPulse.Adapter.sln --locked-mode dotnet build MirrorPulse.Adapter.sln -c Release --no-restore dotnet run --project tests/MirrorPulse.Adapter.ContractTests -c Release --no-build The contract executable validates the SDK and launches the sample Worker. SDK trusted publishing describes how SDK maintainers verify and publish the NuGet package and its companion assets.
